newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News-Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News-Nov 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Overnight leader John Cooper won the Werribee International Three-Day equestrian event yesterday following a clean round in the showjumping. Cooper finished the event with a total of 50.20 penalty points on gelding Falcon Ivory. Page 30.

A head-to-head battle with Super League has been confirmed by the release of the Australian Rugby League's 1997 competition draw. The ARL has scheduled the annual match between Sydney and Country for the same night Super League has planned a Test match between Australian and New Zealand. Page 30.

Wollongong City soccer player Anthony Surjan was sent off with a serious knee injury as the Melbourne Knight's goal-scoring drought continued in the National Soccer League match last night. The match ended in a 0-0 draw. Page 34.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian rugby union Test prop Richard Harry is the fourth Wallaby to return home after he broke his right thumb during a 39-26 victory over Ulster at Ravenhill on Saturday. The break forces him out of contention for the final two Tests of the tour aganst Ireland and Wales. Page 26.

Australian cricket selectors are set to opt for continuity in the team for the first Test against the West Indies, to be announced today, following a weekend of matches posing as trials. With many fringe candidates showing better form than the incumbents the Test will be seen by selectors as the real trial for the remainder of the series. Page 27.

Less than a week before the first of the West Indies cricket Tests, Australia's top-order batsmen Mark Taylor, Michael Slater and Mark Waugh all were bowled out prematurely by Queensland yesterday in New South Wales' inevitable Sheffield Shield defeat. Page 27.
THE AGE

Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco is determined to argue his case against drug charges as strongly as possible to the International Amateur Athletic Federation arbitration panel in Monte Carlo next Sunday. If the panel overturns the decision by the Australian tribunal to clear him, Capobianco faces a four-year ban. Page 2.

The International Olympic Committee has capped athlete numbers for the Sydney Olympics at 10,200 as well as finalising the breakdown of sports for the event. The decision to retain the programme adopted for Atlanta was welcomed by Sydney Olympic organisers. Page 2.

Australian tennis duo Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde have made the final of the Association of Tennis Professionals world doubles championships in Hartford, Connecticut, following the defeat of Byron Black of Zimbabwe and Grant Connell of Canada yesteray. Page 9.
HERALD SUN

AFL plans for 1997 are in turmoil after its draw of games was found to break Carlton's Optus Oval lease. AFL operations manager Ian Collins yesterday said the blunder could waste months of work, and has appealed to the City of Melbourne to change to leas. Page 4.

Lone teenage sailor David Dicks became a national hero yesterday after the completion of his 264 day solo circumnavigation of the world. Dicks achieved his record at on on Saturday after passing the official mark, 11 km norh of Fremantle. Page 7.

Jane Crafter achieved an eagle three and final round five under par 68 to take a dramatic victory on the final green in the Alpine Ladies Masters at Royal Pines golf tournament on Sunday. Crafter is now a two-time winner of the title. Page 76.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Former England soccer coach Terry Venables is set to accept a A$400,000 contract to lead the Australian Socceroo's campaign to qualify for the World Cup. Soccer Australia chief David Hill wants Venables to monitor Australia's European-based players and lead the Socceroo's quest in the Oceania group matches. Page 33.

New South Wales batsman Michael Bevan's international cricket future was under review last night for his reputation of being suspect against the rising ball, after the Ashes series two years ago. His coach Geoff Lawson believes it is an unsound reason for his Test spot to be reviewed. Page 42.

The Sydney Blues' series win over the Hunter Eagles could prove costly with Brendan Kingman and Todd Le Grand facing the Australian Baseball League judiciary today after being ejected at crucial stages of Sydney's win. Page 44.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
